specification.unit_of_analysis: 100–1000 km² subarctic region; sub-region patches 1–10 km²

gotchas_avoided: Resolves patches (30 m pixels cover ~1 km² → detects multi-pixel dams)
NDVI directly measures vegetation change from beaver flooding
Avoids 'temperature → air temp' trap (this is reflectance)
caveats: Does NOT measure subsidence or ground temperature directly
Requires pairing with Sentinel-1 InSAR for subsidence
Arctic cloud cover requires composite strategy (8-day to monthly)
Winter data (snow) not useful; active season June–Sept only
candidates.validation_note: Explicitly listed in Stage 0 'Would Work'; ranked as top choice
candidates.next_step: Pair with Sentinel-1 (rank 2) for subsidence; use regional models for ground temp

gotchas_avoided: Radar penetrates clouds (Arctic advantage over optical)
Avoids 'water from organic soil' confusion (multi-year stacking resolves)
gotchas_hit: Sparse Arctic coverage; not all regions have coherence history
caveats: Does NOT measure vegetation or ground temperature
Requires specialized InSAR processing (Persistent Scatterer or SBAS)
Coherence loss over water/vegetation; seasonal decorrelation
Must be combined with Landsat (rank 1) for vegetation picture
candidates.validation_note: Explicitly listed in Stage 0 'Would Work' for subsidence measurement
candidates.next_step: Use with Landsat for complementary vegetation + subsidence view

specification_fit.latency: MARGINAL (3 weeks OK but not ideal)

gotchas_hit: ⚠️ NAIVE-PICKER TRAP: Keyword search 'permafrost + soil moisture' → SMAP ranks high on relevance
9 km pixel >> 630 m parcel (100× area). Cannot resolve beaver-dam patches.
User doesn't realize they're looking at regional average, not their question
caveats: CRITICAL: Resolution failure. North Slope Borough is 1–2 SMAP pixels total.
Beaver dam impact is 1–10 km² patch; SMAP pixel is 81 km². Cannot detect localized change.
Soil moisture is proxy for permafrost, not direct measurement
candidates.validation_note: Exemplifies the 'naive-picker trap': high relevance score, wrong scale entirely
candidates.next_step: DO NOT USE for this question. Use Landsat + Sentinel-1 instead.

recommendation.approach: Multi-layer strategy: (1) Landsat vegetation time series (NDVI 2013–2026) for beaver-dam detection. (2) Sentinel-1 InSAR stack (2014–2026) for subsidence measurement. (3) Regional permafrost models (NSIDC, UiO) for ground temperature. This gives full picture of beaver-driven permafrost changes.
data_gaps: Ground temperature: Satellite cannot measure directly. Requires NSIDC ground-temp models or in-situ permafrost stations.
Ice richness (pore-space ice): No satellite observable. Only cores/boreholes access this.
recommendation.confidence: High (0.92). Top candidates align with Stage 0 'Would Work' predictions. SMAP correctly identified as naive trap despite keyword relevance.

stage_3_exploration_spec.test_region: North Slope Borough, Alaska (bbox: -157 to -156.5°W, 68 to 68.5°N)
stage_3_exploration_spec.test_method: Time series analysis 2015–2026. NDVI anomaly detection for vegetation change; InSAR subsidence stacking.
exploratory_queries: How does Landsat NDVI change correlate with known beaver activity (2015–2020)?
Can we detect vegetation signature of beaver dams (flooding + shrub expansion)?
Does Sentinel-1 InSAR show subsidence in active beaver regions?
What is the signal-to-noise ratio (subsidence vs. seasonal/thermal noise)?
success_criteria: NDVI time series shows detectable change (Δ ≥ 0.1) in beaver-active areas
InSAR stack coherence ≥ 0.6 over 5+ years in permafrost regions
Subsidence signal ≥ 5 mm/year emerges above thermal/seasonal noise
Change detection matches ground-truth beaver sightings (if available)
expected_gotchas: Arctic cloud cover (need composite strategy, 4–8 week windows)
Winter data useless (snow masking); June–September only
InSAR coherence loss over water/wet tundra in melt season
Permafrost creep (natural subsidence) as noise; need multi-year stack to separate beaver-driven change
